---
title: "Follow-up forms are reports, not events"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE
)
```

SRTR follow-up files (`TXF_KI`, `TXF_LI`, and so on) hold one row per
follow-up form. It is tempting to read them as a clinical record: find the
first form that says "yes", take its date, and call that the event. That
reading is wrong in several ways, and each one quietly changes an
analysis. This article walks through them with code you can run on your own
standard analysis files (SAFs). The companion article,
[Follow-up windows and death](follow-up-windows.html), covers what happens
around the end of follow-up and death.

The code here is not run on this website, because it needs real SAFs. You
can run it yourself: each section shows a naive version first, then the
sRtr function that handles the problem. When you share what you find,
share counts only, and mask any count under 11, as the SRTR data use
agreement requires. The `mask()` helper below does that for a table.

```{r setup}
library(sRtr)
library(dplyr)

set_srtr_wd("path/to/your/SAFs")

tx <- load_srtr_file("TX_LI")
txf <- load_srtr_file(
  "TXF_LI",
  col_select = c(
    "TRR_ID", "ORG_TY", "TFL_PX_STAT_DT", "TFL_FOL_CD",
    "TFL_MALIG", "TFL_ACUTE_REJ_EPISODE"
  )
)

mask <- function(x) {
  t <- table(x, useNA = "ifany")
  noquote(ifelse(t > 0 & t < 11, "<11", format(t, big.mark = ",")))
}
```

The examples use liver files and malignancy and acute rejection, the two
outcomes `add_txf_outcomes()` derives. The same issues apply to the other
organs.

# A form date is not an onset date

Each follow-up form covers a period, often a year, and its date
(`TFL_PX_STAT_DT`, the patient status date) is when the status was
recorded. A form that first says "yes, malignancy" tells you the malignancy
began at some point after the last form that said "no", and on or before
this one. The figure below shows three made-up recipients.

```{r timeline, eval = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 2.8, fig.alt = "Timeline of follow-up forms for three made-up recipients, in years since transplant. Recipient A has forms saying no at years 1 and 2 and yes at year 3; the onset lies somewhere in the shaded interval between years 2 and 3. Recipient B has a form saying no at year 1, an unknown answer at year 2 and yes at year 3; the onset interval runs from year 1 to year 3. Recipient C has forms saying unknown at years 1 and 2, so nothing is known about malignancy."}
forms <- data.frame(
  who = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), c(3, 3, 2)),
  year = c(1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1, 2),
  answer = c("No", "No", "Yes", "No", "Unknown", "Yes", "Unknown", "Unknown")
)
forms$answer <- factor(forms$answer, c("No", "Yes", "Unknown"))
intervals <- data.frame(who = c("A", "B"), from = c(2, 1), to = c(3, 3))
ink <- "#52514e"

ggplot2::ggplot(forms, ggplot2::aes(x = year, y = who)) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    data = intervals,
    ggplot2::aes(x = from, xend = to, y = who, yend = who),
    linewidth = 6, colour = "#cde2fb", lineend = "round"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = ink, linewidth = 0.4) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    ggplot2::aes(colour = answer, shape = answer),
    size = 3.5, stroke = 1.2
  ) +
  ggplot2::annotate(
    "text", x = 0.05, y = 3.45, label = "Transplant",
    hjust = 0, size = 3.2, colour = ink
  ) +
  ggplot2::annotate(
    "text", x = 2.5, y = 3.32, label = "Onset is somewhere in here",
    size = 3.2, colour = ink
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(No = "#2a78d6", Yes = "#eb6834", Unknown = "#8a8984"),
    name = "Form says"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(No = 16, Yes = 17, Unknown = 1),
    name = "Form says"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(limits = c("C", "B", "A")) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    "Years since transplant", breaks = 0:3, limits = c(0, 3.2)
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(y = "Recipient") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left"
  )
```

**The naive approach** takes the first "yes":

```{r}
naive <- txf |>
  filter(TFL_MALIG == "Y") |>
  summarise(malig_date = min(TFL_PX_STAT_DT), .by = TRR_ID)
```

This gives the date of the first *report*, which lags onset by up to the
gap between forms. It also has a technical trap: `min()` returns `NA` for a
recipient whose positive forms include an undated one, and with
`na.rm = TRUE` it returns `Inf`, with a warning, when all of them are
undated.

**With sRtr**, `add_txf_outcomes()` gives the first report date and the
other end of the interval: the last form that explicitly said "no" before
it.

```{r}
tx <- add_txf_outcomes(tx)

gap <- as.numeric(tx$FIRST_FU_MALIG_DATE - tx$FIRST_FU_MALIG_LAST_NEG_DATE)
summary(gap)
```

On real files the median gap is close to a year, because forms are mostly
annual. An analysis that treats the report date as the event date is
right-censored data with a built-in delay; the two dates together support
interval-censored or discrete-time models instead. Even then, the interval
bounds the onset only as well as the form's question does: the forms ask
about the period since the last form, and are filled in from the
transplant center's records.

# A missing date does not mean "no event"

**The naive approach** joins the first dates back to the cohort and calls
everyone without one event-free:

```{r}
naive_cohort <- tx |>
  left_join(naive, by = "TRR_ID") |>
  mutate(malignancy = !is.na(malig_date))
```

That merges four quite different groups into "no malignancy":

- recipients whose forms said "no";
- recipients whose forms said only "unknown" or were left blank;
- recipients with no follow-up form at all;
- recipients with a "yes" form that has no date.

**With sRtr**, the status column keeps them apart:

```{r}
mask(tx$FIRST_FU_MALIG_STATUS)
```

`"event"` means at least one form reports a malignancy, dated or not;
`"no event"` means none does and at least one says "no"; `"unknown"` means
there are forms but none says "yes" or "no"; `"no follow-up"` means there is
no form. On real liver files, "unknown" and "no follow-up" are each large
groups, not rounding errors. Whether to exclude them, treat them as
censored at transplant, or model them is an analysis decision, and it
should be made on purpose.

# "Rejection" has more than one meaning

The rejection question (`TFL_ACUTE_REJ_EPISODE`, format `ACREJEPF`) has
four answers: 1, at least one episode treated with an anti-rejection
agent; 2, rejection, none treated; 3, no; 998, unknown.

**The naive approach** matches the label text:

```{r}
txf |>
  filter(
    TFL_ACUTE_REJ_EPISODE ==
      "1: Yes, at least one episode treated with anti-rejection agent"
  )
```

This finds nothing if the file was loaded with raw codes
(`factor_labels = FALSE`), and nothing if SRTR rewords the label in a later
release. And it treats an untreated rejection (code 2) the same as "no".

**With sRtr**, rejection is matched by code, so raw and labelled files give
the same answer, and an untreated rejection gets its own status:

```{r}
mask(tx$FIRST_FU_REJ_STATUS)
```

The derived endpoint is *treated* acute rejection. An untreated rejection
is evidence that rejection happened, so it is never used as a negative form
when bounding the interval in `FIRST_FU_REJ_LAST_NEG_DATE`.

# Rejection during the transplant admission is not on the follow-up forms

Rejection before discharge is recorded on the transplant record
(`REC_ACUTE_REJ_EPISODE` in `TX_LI`), not on a follow-up form, and it has
no date of its own.

**The naive approach** uses only the follow-up file, and so misses early
rejection, or counts it late, at the first follow-up form.

**With sRtr**, `add_time_to_event_outcomes()` (see the note in
[Follow-up windows and death](follow-up-windows.html)) uses the admission
rejection first. It
dates it at discharge, a proxy: the transplant date plus the length of stay
(`REC_POSTX_LOS`), else the discharge date (`REC_DISCHRG_DT`).
`FIRST_REJ_DATE_SOURCE` records which rule applied:

```{r}
out <- sRtr:::add_time_to_event_outcomes(tx)
mask(out$FIRST_REJ_DATE_SOURCE)
```

When neither date is usable, the rejection still counts: its status is 1
and its time is missing, so it drops out of a survival model rather than
adding rejection-free time. The same rule covers a rejection or malignancy
reported only on undated follow-up forms. Each case gives a warning with
the count.

# Forms can be dated before the transplant

A follow-up form describes the period after transplant, so a form dated
before it is a data error. Check how many you have:

```{r}
tx_date <- tx$REC_TX_DT[match(txf$TRR_ID, tx$TRR_ID)]
sum(txf$TFL_PX_STAT_DT < tx_date, na.rm = TRUE)
```

In liver files they are rare, but a single one can matter: with the naive
approach, a pre-transplant "yes" becomes an event at time zero, or a
negative time. sRtr times events from the first report on or after the
transplant date; the date columns from `add_txf_outcomes()` keep the first
report of all, so you can find these cases.

# Count registrations, and say so

Each row of a transplant file is a transplant registration (`TRR_ID`), not
a person. A person transplanted twice has two rows, and two sets of
follow-up forms.

```{r}
c(registrations = n_distinct(tx$TRR_ID), people = n_distinct(tx$PERS_ID))
```

`add_txf_outcomes()` attaches a report of the merge, in registrations,
ready for a methods section: how many registrations have any follow-up
form, how many forms were read and how many were undated, and for each
outcome the positive forms, the registrations with a report, and the
registrations whose report is dated.

```{r}
report <- attr(tx, "txf_report")
str(report[setdiff(names(report), "outcomes")])
report$outcomes
```

The report describes the cohort at the time of the merge; filter first,
then call `add_txf_outcomes()`, if you want it to describe your analysis
cohort.

# Checklist

- Treat follow-up dates as report dates. Use the last negative form as the
  other end of the interval.
- Read the status column before treating a missing date as no event.
- Decide what "unknown" and "no follow-up" mean for your question.
- Match codes, not label text, and decide whether untreated rejection
  counts.
- Include rejection during the transplant admission.
- Look for forms dated before the transplant.
- Report counts in registrations, and mask counts under 11 when you share
  them.
